items.text:
Only finished the tutorial/intro after reading up on the forums a bit. 

It took me two tries to finish it, coz the tutorial that gets you to do a single scavenge "loop": [ gear up, get to your ship, undock, get to derelict, dock, change to pressure suit, scavenge, get back, sell stuff] is all subject to a scavenge license that you find on the derelict (you normally have to buy a license on the station). 

That "free" "tutorial" license doesn't last long. You got about an hour or two (normally the minimum duration sold is 24h), and that, considering someone who is completely new to the game, is not enough. 

So advice to devs, extend that for a few hours. Four more hours should do it to cover most type of players. That was how long past due I was after my first try, after I got back and basically couldn't sell anything worth making any ends meet, coz the license had expired. 

There is also a scrap vendor that is always available but they don't always want the stuff you got.  And there is also a fence (black market) but you need to become friends with him, but he wants rare stuff i expect. He does update more frequently though, I hear.

Anyway on to the review:

The good: 
Its immersive and given past experience the devs had (Neo Scavenger) I expect it to be deep enough in its social complexity too. It was certainly attractive to me, when it comes to technical depth, got plenty of it. It does feel realistic, doing the salvage, flying the ship etc, so that is a huge plus. 

The bad:
It takes some getting used to, the mechanics, but having said that they are not that difficult to pick up and feel second nature quickly enough

The ugly:
Its pixel graphics. but again having said that, its quite advanced pixel graphics. 

For example ship parts from Walls and Floors to Thrusters, Batteries and Nav Consoles can be repaired and restored. After a while I expect you will get used to what they look like, so you recognize them easy. While repairing them doesn't seem to do much in terms of looks, restoring them does. So as you restore something, the icon representing that thing becomes a lot clearer. Un-restored, a yellow floor will be sprinkled with different shades of yellow or even nearby colors, making it almost unrecognizable. A whole ship like that, and its seems a blur of pixels. You don't know what's what. But once you start restoring stuff, it takes shape. Makes you want to do it. Quite smart that, as a game-mechanic. 




Also the game makes smart use of time flow. Depending on skill, it will take sometime to install/uninstall, repair or restore something. Enter the time controls, recommended even. Just fast forward time.

Speaking of skills there is a random process of choice at the character creation stage. Think Oxygen Not Included or Rimworld.

 Its pretty much set at the moment and people who played, have figured out what's what and there are excellent guides (kudos) in the guide section here on Steam. 

However as part of the game, it feels like people will end up re-rolling characters. Its interesting coz there are ways to advance most of the skills, even get rid of bad traits, by playing in-game, but still everyone will look to get better skills and so re-roll to get a better experience. 

For example installing, uninstalling, repairing, restoring, this stuff takes time, depending on skill. Unless there is a particular challenge to track, i.e. hard mode, something to brag about, there is no reason anyone would not get that running-start on skills, at character creation, coz some of them all they do is reduce the time you spend fast-forwarding time to get the particular task done, not to mention you save on oxygen, or more like when the suit-CO2 alarm goes off and you have to get back to the ship to remove and put back your helmet to get fresh air in the suit.

But even with all those quirks, overall, it's one of those games that you feel you got your moneys worth. It also checks the primary 'what-is-a-game-and-what-is-it-for' boxes for me, namely, education (getting to know how the world works (like coal and iron makes steel ) and get to know yourself too (stuff like risk, greed, handling failure but success too) and immersion, so yes, highly recommended.
items.text_zh:
在论坛上稍微查了点资料后，我才刚刚完成教程/序章。

我试了两次才完成，因为那个让你做一次拾荒“循环”的教程：[装备好，到你的飞船，脱离对接，到达废弃飞船，对接，换上压力服，拾荒，返回，卖东西] 全都受制于你在废弃飞船上找到的拾荒许可证（通常你必须在空间站上购买许可证）。

那个“免费”的“教程”许可证持续不了多久。你大约只有一两个小时（通常出售的最短时长是24小时），而且，考虑到一个完全新接触这款游戏的人，这并不够。

所以给开发者的建议是，把它延长几个小时。再多四个小时应该就足以覆盖大多数类型的玩家了。我第一次尝试后，超时了那么久，回来后基本上什么都卖不出去，没法维持生计，因为许可证已经过期了。

还有一个总是可用的废料商贩，但他们并不总是想要你拿到的东西。另外还有一个销赃人（黑市），但你需要和他成为朋友，不过我猜他想要稀有的东西。不过，我听说他更新得更频繁。

总之，进入评测：

优点：
它很有沉浸感，而且鉴于开发者过去的经验（Neo Scavenger），我预计它在社会复杂性方面也足够有深度。就技术深度而言，它确实很吸引我，这方面内容很丰富。它确实感觉真实，做打捞、驾驶飞船等等，所以这是一个巨大的加分项。

缺点：
机制需要一些时间来适应，但话虽如此，它们并不难上手，很快就能感觉像第二天性一样。

丑陋之处：
它是像素画面。但话又说回来，它是相当先进的像素画面。

例如，从墙壁和地板到推进器、电池和导航控制台的飞船部件都可以修理和修复。过一段时间，我预计你会习惯它们的样子，这样你就能轻松认出它们。虽然修理它们在外观上似乎没什么变化，但修复它们就有变化。所以当你修复某样东西时，代表那东西的图标会变得清晰得多。未修复时，一块黄色的地板会散布着不同深浅的黄色甚至相近的颜色，让它几乎无法辨认。整艘飞船都那样，看起来就是一团模糊的像素。你不知道什么是什么。但一旦你开始修复东西，它就成形了。让你想要去做。作为游戏机制，这相当聪明。




另外，游戏巧妙地利用了时间流逝。根据技能不同，安装/卸载、修理或修复某样东西会花一些时间。进入时间控制，甚至推荐这么做。直接快进时间。

说到技能，在角色创建阶段有一个随机选择过程。想想《缺氧》或《环世界》。

目前它基本上已经定型，玩过的人已经弄清楚了什么是什么，而且在Steam这里的指南区有很棒的指南（致敬）。

然而，作为游戏的一部分，感觉人们最终会重掷角色。这很有趣，因为有一些方法可以通过在游戏中游玩来提升大多数技能，甚至摆脱坏特质，但每个人仍然会寻求更好的技能，所以会重掷以获得更好的体验。

例如安装、卸载、修理、修复，这些东西会花时间，取决于技能。除非有某个特定的挑战要追踪，比如困难模式，某种可以吹嘘的东西，否则任何人都没有理由不去获得那种……
在角色创建时就让技能有个抢先起步的优势，因为其中一些技能的作用只是减少你花在快进时间来完成特定任务上的时间，更不用说还能节省氧气，或者更准确地说，是当宇航服的二氧化碳警报响起、你不得不返回飞船摘下再戴回头盔，好让宇航服里换进新鲜空气的时候。

但即便有所有这些怪毛病，总体而言，这是那种让你觉得钱花得值的游戏之一。它也为我勾选了首要的“什么是游戏、游戏是为了什么”的选项，也就是教育（了解世界如何运转（比如煤和铁炼成钢）以及了解你自己（诸如风险、贪婪、应对失败，但也要应对成功之类的东西））和沉浸感，所以是的，强烈推荐。
